name: Adenosarcoma of the cervix uteri
aliases: Mixed Müllerian tumor of the cervix

criteria.description: Presence of biphasic tumor with benign epithelial and malignant stromal components
Increased mitotic activity in stromal component (>2 mitoses per 10 high-power fields)
Subepithelial condensation of stromal cells (cambium layer) beneath benign glands
Immunohistochemical positivity for CD10 in stromal cells and estrogen/progesterone receptor expression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of biphasic tumor with malignant stromal component and increased mitotic activity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other mixed Müllerian tumors and sarcomas of the cervix

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cervical mass detected on pelvic examination

searchTerms: low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia due to chronic blood loss

rare.symptomName: Fistula formation between cervix and adjacent organs
searchTerms: abnormal passage between cervix and nearby organs

rare.symptomName: Lower extremity edema due to lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: lower limb edema due to lymphatic obstruction

laboratory: Mild anemia on complete blood count
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing heterogeneous cervical mass
MRI pelvis demonstrating polypoid cervical lesion with stromal invasion
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; some cases show alterations in TP53 and MDM2
other: Histopathology revealing biphasic tumor with benign glands and malignant stroma
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD10 and hormone receptors in stromal cells

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly malignant mesenchymal cells without benign epithelial component
Desmin and myogenin positive on immunohistochemistry
Tumor located in uterine corpus rather than cervix
Similar histology but different anatomical site
Benign stromal component without significant mitotic activity
Lack of stromal atypia and invasion

redFlags: Persistent abnormal vaginal bleeding despite treatment
Pelvic pain associated with cervical lesion
references: Kurman RJ, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs. 4th Edition. IARC; 2014.
Orphanet Report on Adenosarcoma of the Cervix Uteri, ORPHA:213792.
McCluggage WG. Uterine adenosarcoma: a review. Int J Gynecol Pathol. 2006;25(4): 313-324.
